title: [finding] `GET /meta/<unknown-type>/<name>` says "item not found" — the single-item 404 cannot tell an unknown TYPE from an unknown ITEM
body:
Found while implementing #9488 (the list door's unknown-type refusal). Filed unassigned; not fixed there, because #9488's scope is the LIST door and this door does not carry #9488's defect — it already refuses distinguishably.

## Observed

Measured on `packages/rest`'s `GET /api/v1/meta/:type/:name` with a type name that is in neither the static spelling contract nor any live registry:

```
GET /api/v1/meta/totally_invented_type/x
  -> 404 {"error":"Metadata item totally_invented_type/x not found","code":"RESOURCE_NOT_FOUND"}
```

The producer is `@objectstack/metadata-protocol`'s `protocol.ts` (`Metadata item ${type}/${name} not found`).

## Why it is worth recording

This is a **weaker form** of what #9488 was filed about, not an instance of it — and the difference is why this is an observation rather than a bug:

- #9488's defect was **indistinguishable from success**: `200` with an empty collection reads exactly like "this type exists and holds nothing".
- This answer is a refusal, so a caller cannot mistake it for a served result. Nothing is silently wrong.

What it does do is **point the caller at the wrong half of the address**. The write door for the same segment says *"'totally_invented_type' is not a metadata type"*; this door says the **item** was not found, for a request whose actual mistake was the **type**. A caller who typo'd the type re-checks the name — the one thing that cannot help them, which is the same shape recorded on the repeated-filter refusal (a message naming the wrong cause sends the reader to re-check the part that was already correct).

The three doors therefore give three different accounts of one segment:

| door | answer for an unknown type name |
|---|---|
| `PUT /meta/:type/:name` | `400` `INVALID_REQUEST` — "'x' is not a metadata type" |
| `GET /meta/:type` (after #9488) | `400` `INVALID_REQUEST` — same sentence, same code |
| `GET /meta/:type/:name` | `404` `RESOURCE_NOT_FOUND` — "Metadata item x/y not found" |

## What a fix would have to respect, if one is wanted

The same constraint #9488 measured, and it is the reason this is not a one-line change:

- the refusal cannot be raised from the static spelling contract alone. `unrecognisedMetaTypeRefusal` returns a verdict for `data`, `kind`, `package` and `policy` — live `SchemaRegistry` keys an ordinary `registerApp` produces and `GET /meta/types` enumerates — and for plugin types, which enter the live set by registering items. Refusing on the static half alone would answer `400` for types this same service advertises, which is the objection recorded when the write-side verdict landed and was deliberately not raised on the read entries then.
- so it needs the same union #9488 built for the list door (static contract ∪ live listing), and a decision about whether a **type**-level refusal should outrank the item-level `404` on an address where both are true.

No consumer is known to depend on the current wording; the sweep behind #9488 found no caller addressing an off-contract type on this route outside refusal fixtures.

## Not covered by

- #9180 (`/meta` type segment is always singular) — that ruling is about **plural spellings**, a different axis.
- #9488 — the list door only; the single-item doors were measured and explicitly left alone there.

No priority and no `domain:*` label — normal triage first-touch.
